subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting remain Gateway-internal with restart accounting, or should OpenClaw add an external watchdog or ledger path that reports started-but-not-completed cron runs even when the Gateway event loop is wedged?
rationale: Source inspection can show current restart accounting and in-process alerts, but choosing an external or supervisor-backed alerting contract affects product behavior, operator expectations, and macOS service design.

options.title: Add external stuck-run reporting
options.body: Define a supervisor or persistent ledger path that records cron start and success, then reports timeout or interruption after restart without relying on the wedged Gateway event loop.

options.title: Keep restart-only accounting
options.body: Treat current startup interrupted-run recovery as sufficient and require only memory-leak/root-cause validation before closing.

options.title: Split memory and alerting
options.body: Track memory growth separately from failure-alert durability so the leak fix can land independently of the alerting product decision.

recommendation.title: Add external stuck-run reporting
recommendation.body: Define a supervisor or persistent ledger path that records cron start and success, then reports timeout or interruption after restart without relying on the wedged Gateway event loop.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron service and failure-alert refactoring makes steipete the best history-backed owner for the alerting semantics decision.
